unitTargets: ▸  I can tell distance from displacement and speed from velocity, using signs.
▸  I can calculate acceleration and choose the right kinematic equation.
▸  I can read velocity, acceleration and displacement off motion graphs.
▸  I can solve free-fall problems with a = −9.81 m/s², taking up as positive.
keyTerms: ▸  Average speed, average velocity, instantaneous velocity
▸  Acceleration, kinematic equation, free fall, g
howItWorks: The left column holds the questions you should be able to answer from the notes beside them. Cover the right side and quiz yourself with it later.
A line with a gold rule down its left edge is must-write. Copy it exactly.
Every worked example has a bordered work area. Show enough that I can follow your reasoning, and carry units the whole way.

sectionsContent.title: Distance, Displacement & Velocity
sectionsContent.learningTarget: I can tell distance from displacement and speed from velocity, and I can use the sign of a number to state a direction.

cues: What do you have to choose before any position number means anything?
What does the sign of a position tell you?
notes: Position x is where an object is, measured from a chosen  __________ .
Before writing any number, you choose an origin and a  _______________________________ .
The sign of a position tells you which  _______  of zero the object is on. It does not mean fast or slow.
Displacement Δx = final position − initial position.  Above: Δx = (+20 m) − (−10 m) =  _________ .

cues: Which one can be negative?
A runner does one full lap. What is the displacement?
rows.notesLabel: TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS ABOUT THE SAME TRIP
notes: Distance is the total  ___________________  travelled. It is a scalar and it is never negative.
Displacement is the change in position,  ________________________________ . It is a vector, so it carries a sign.
Runner: 120 m east, then 45 m west. Distance =  _________ .  Displacement =  _________ .

cues: Which of the two needs a direction?
When are the two numbers equal?
notes: average speed =  ______________  ÷ total time      (scalar)
average velocity =  ____________________  ÷ total time      (vector)
They are equal only when the motion never  _____________________________ .
Instantaneous velocity is the velocity at  _________________  — what a photogate estimates over a very short distance.

cues: What is the first thing written down, before any number?

problem.label: EXAMPLE — A TRIP WITH A TURNAROUND
problem.statement: A student walks 40. m east from the door, turns, and walks 15 m west. The trip takes 22 s. Take east as positive.
problem.given: leg 1 = 40. m east · leg 2 = 15 m west · Δt = 22 s
problem.need: distance · displacement · average speed · average velocity

sectionsContent.summaryPrompt: In your own words: two students take different routes from the door to the flagpole and arrive at the same time. What must be the same about their trips, and what can be different?
selfCheck: I can state the positive direction before I start a problem.
I can find distance and displacement for a trip with a turnaround.
I can say why average speed and average velocity can differ.

sectionsContent.title: Acceleration & the Kinematic Equations
sectionsContent.learningTarget: I can calculate acceleration from a change in velocity, and I can choose the kinematic equation that fits the givens.

cues: What exactly is changing when something accelerates?
What do the units m/s² actually mean, in words?
notes: a = Δv ÷ Δt — the change in  ______________  divided by the time it took.
Units: m/s per second, written  _______ . In words: every second, the velocity changes by that many m/s.
Acceleration is a vector, so it carries a  _______ .
Equal time between dots. Spacing that grows means the object is  ___________________ .

cues: Does a negative acceleration always mean slowing down?
Give one case where both v and a are negative.
rows.notesLabel: COMPARING THE SIGN OF a TO THE SIGN OF v
notes: Same signs → the object  _______________ .  Opposite signs → the object  _________________ .

cues: Which quantity does each equation leave out?
What must be true about a for these to work?
notes: A zero subscript marks a starting value: v₀ is the velocity at the start, v is the velocity at time t.

cues: Why does part (b) not need the acceleration?

problem.label: EXAMPLE — MERGING ONTO THE HIGHWAY
problem.statement: A car on an entrance ramp speeds up from 12 m/s to 26 m/s in 5.0 s. Direction of travel is positive.
problem.given: v₀ = 12 m/s · v = 26 m/s · Δt = 5.0 s
problem.need: (a) acceleration    (b) distance covered on the ramp

cues: Which given is missing here, and which equation does that point to?

problem.label: EXAMPLE — NO TIME GIVEN
problem.statement: A cart enters a 24 m stretch of track at 3.0 m/s and speeds up at a steady 1.5 m/s². Find its velocity at the end of the stretch.
problem.given: v₀ = 3.0 m/s · a = 1.5 m/s² · Δx = 24 m
problem.need: v at the end of the stretch
problem.workLabel: WORK — TAKE THE SQUARE ROOT LAST

sectionsContent.summaryPrompt: In your own words: how do you decide which of the four equations to use, without trying all four?
selfCheck: I can calculate acceleration and give it a sign.
I can say when a negative acceleration speeds something up.
I can pick the right kinematic equation from the givens.

sectionsContent.title: Position, Velocity & Acceleration Graphs
sectionsContent.learningTarget: I can read velocity, acceleration and displacement off motion graphs, and I can sketch all three graphs for a described motion.

cues: What quantity is the slope?
What does a flat line mean?
notes: Slope = rise ÷ run = Δx ÷ Δt, which has units of  _______  — so the slope is the  ______________ .
Straight line → constant velocity. Curved line → the velocity is  ______________ , so there is an acceleration.
A flat line means the object is  ____________  — not that it is at the origin.

cues: What quantity is the slope?
What quantity is the area?
rows.notesLabel: SLOPE AND AREA ON A VELOCITY–TIME GRAPH
notes: Slope = Δv ÷ Δt, in (m/s) per s, so the slope is the  ____________________ .
Area = height × width = (m/s)(s) = m, so the area is the  ____________________ .
Break the shape into triangles and rectangles, then add. Area below the time axis counts as  ______________  displacement.

cues: Sketch all three graphs for a cart moving at constant speed.
Which row is a straight line in all three?
notes: Constant velocity: x–t straight, v–t flat, a–t at  _______ .
Constant acceleration: x–t curved, v–t  ______________ , a–t flat but not zero.
Changing acceleration: a–t is itself a  __________  line.

cues: Why is no kinematic equation needed here?

problem.label: EXAMPLE — READING A VELOCITY–TIME GRAPH
problem.statement: A cart speeds up from rest to 8.0 m/s in 4.0 s, holds 8.0 m/s for 3.0 s, then slows to rest in 2.0 s.
problem.given: leg A: 0 → 8.0 m/s in 4.0 s · leg B: 8.0 m/s for 3.0 s · leg C: 8.0 → 0 in 2.0 s
problem.need: (a) acceleration during leg A    (b) total displacement

sectionsContent.summaryPrompt: In your own words: a cart's x–t graph rises, levels off, then falls. Describe what the cart actually did, in three steps.
selfCheck: I can find velocity from the slope of an x–t graph.
I can find displacement from the area under a v–t graph.
I can sketch all three graphs from a written description.

sectionsContent.title: Free Fall
sectionsContent.learningTarget: I can solve vertical motion problems using a = −9.81 m/s² with up as the positive direction.

cues: What has to be true for an object to be in free fall?
Why does mass not appear in the answer?
notes: Free fall means  ____________  is the only force acting — no air resistance, no push, no string.
Thrown up, thrown down, or dropped: all free fall once  ______________ .
g = 9.81 m/s² downward. Taking up as positive, a =  _________________  for the whole flight.

cues: At the very top, what is v? What is a?
How does the time up compare with the time down?
notes: At the top of the flight v =  _______ , but a is still  _________________ . It never stops accelerating.
Between the same two heights, the time up equals the time  _______ .
Thrown up at +18.0 m/s, it returns to that height at  _______________ .

cues: Which given comes from the phrase "at the top"?

problem.label: EXAMPLE — THROWN STRAIGHT UP
problem.statement: A ball is thrown straight up from a student's hand at 18.0 m/s. Up is positive.
problem.given: v₀ = +18.0 m/s · a = −9.81 m/s² · at the top, v = 0
problem.need: (a) time to reach the top    (b) height gained above the hand

cues: Why is the displacement negative here?

problem.label: EXAMPLE — DROPPED FROM A CLIFF
problem.statement: A rock is dropped from the top of a 45.0 m cliff. Up is positive and the cliff top is the origin.
problem.need: (a) time to reach the ground    (b) velocity on impact
problem.answer: Answers: t =  __________  and v =  _______________ , meaning 29.7 m/s downward.

sectionsContent.summaryPrompt: In your own words: a ball is thrown straight up. Explain what happens to its velocity and to its acceleration on the way up, at the top, and on the way down.
selfCheck: I can state a = −9.81 m/s² and say why it is negative.
I can explain why v = 0 at the top but a is not.
I can solve a dropped-object problem with the right sign on Δx.

close.bigPicture: Trace one motion all the way through: position, velocity, acceleration, and what each graph of it looks like.
